pullRequests.title: Item randomizer: add optional New Game+ start for RAC1
pullRequests.author: SavedbyBlood9
pullRequests.head: feat/item-randomizer-new-game-plus
pullRequests.body:
Adds a RAC1-only launcher setting, Start in New Game+ (start_in_new_game_plus), off by default. When enabled, a randomized save uses the retail New Game+ mode flag and Goodies menu, matching Archipelago's behavior without granting gold weapons or completed-save inventory.
The option respects the existing seed/save gate, leaves foreign saves and the front end alone, and never downgrades an already-earned New Game+ save when disabled. It is selected separately from seed codes, so existing item…

pullRequests.title: Archipelago: separate shuffled gold-case purchase and shop access fixes
pullRequests.author: SavedbyBlood9
pullRequests.head: feat/archipelago-gold-case-access
pullRequests.body:
Shuffled gold cases can be purchased without owning the original base weapon, while retaining both retail currency costs. The temporary ownership view is restored for save serialization. Enabling shuffle_gold_weapons also opens the Novalis shop teleporter and full stock without requiring or enabling New Game+.
The Archipelago gold-weapon pool, server option, APWorld generation, currency accounting and save checks already exist on master. This PR isolates the remaining gold-case gameplay changes…

pullRequests.title: Item randomizer: add optional gold-weapon case shuffle pool
pullRequests.author: SavedbyBlood9
pullRequests.head: feat/item-randomizer-gold-cases
pullRequests.body:
Adds the RAC1 launcher switch Shuffle gold-weapon cases (shuffle_gold_weapons, off by default). The ten gold upgrades and purchase locations join the selected item pools. The Novalis shop opens without New Game+, and purchases retain the normal bolt price plus four Gold Bolts without requiring ownership of the original base weapon. Receiving a gold weapon grants its base weapon and upgrade.
Gold Bolt currency and progression items stay outside cases. Separate saved checks track purchases…

pullRequests.author: farfeduc
pullRequests.head: feat/cheats-overlay
pullRequests.body:
cheats 0.4.0: the same switches and buttons as the pause page, in OpenRAC's own menu, at any time in the game. Still interface 1.12 and the pinned SDK; one commit on master.

OpenRAC's in-game menu has listed mods' menus (developer_menu, interface 1.10) since #211, the menu shared by desktop and Android. It opens with Alt, Start+Select, or the drawer on a touch screen. Picking a planet flies there as from the ship, backing out carries on where you were, and picking the current planet restarts its level. pullRequests.title: Show NPC reward names in interaction prompts for both RAC1 randomizers
pullRequests.author: SavedbyBlood9
pullRequests.head: feat/rac1-npc-reward-text
pullRequests.body:
NPC purchase prompts replace the vanilla reward name with the randomized item; other handoff prompts append Reward: <item>. Archipelago uses the scouted item, omitting the recipient for local rewards and retaining it for other players. Until scouting arrives it uses Unscouted reward. The item randomizer uses the seed's placement. Native prices, buttons and format arguments remain intact, and long prompts wrap inside the panel.

pullRequests.title: fix(difficulty): include <algorithm> in the pool test
pullRequests.author: farfeduc
pullRequests.head: fix/difficulty-pool-test-include
pullRequests.body:
difficulty-mod/tests/pool_test.cpp calls std::fill without including <algorithm>. Other standard libraries bring it in through <vector>, but llvm-mingw's libc++ does not, so difficulty_pool_test did not compile with it:
difficulty-mod/tests/pool_test.cpp:44:10: error: no member named 'fill' in namespace 'std'

One line, in the test only; the mod itself is unchanged.
Tested: the file compiles with llvm-mingw's clang++ (C++17).
